newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy faces chaotic two weeks of transport strikes.
newsitem.headline: Italy faces chaotic two weeks of transport strikes.

text.p: Air traffic controllers went on strike at 11 Italian airports on Monday at the start of what are set to be two chaotic weeks of stoppages by transport workers locked in contract disputes.

Monday's eight-hour strike was unlikely to paralyse air traffic at Bari, Bologna, Cagliari, Catania, Genova, Milan Malpensa, Naples, Bergamo, Palermo, Trieste and Turin since it was called by smaller controllers' unions.
But big delays were expected as a result of another planned eight-hour air traffic controllers strike on Wednesday called by six main labour organisations.
Bus, tram and metro drivers were planning a national stoppage on Thursday, followed next Monday by a four-day strike by petrol pump attendants.

Another strike by air traffic controllers was planned in Milan for Friday April 18 and a four-day sea transport strike was due to start on April 19. Railway workers have also called a 24-hour stoppage from the evening of April 19.
Transport Minister Claudio Burlando said he hoped dialogue would prevail. "We're hoping to reach a deal with the unions," he said at the weekend.
